chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub al-Kub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not befitting for anyone to take from the soil of what is around the Ka'bah. And if he takes anything from that, he should return it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking soil from around the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the ruling of *istihbāb* (preference) or *wujūb* (obligation) regarding the soil surrounding the Ka'bah, distinguishing it from the sacred precincts where removal is prohibited. The chain of narration (*isnād*) reflects the rigorous transmission methods of the Kufan scholars, while the practical implication emphasizes preserving the sanctity of the site by ensuring the earth remains in its place. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and reverence for the physical spaces associated with divine worship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Dawood Bin Al Numan, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is not befitting for anyone that he take from the soil of what is around the Kabah. And if he does take anything from that, he should return it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu’man from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘
It is not proper to take soil from around al- Ka‘bah, and if one does so he must return it back.’”
